description: One column passing a HIGH signal or a LOW signal under a gate, with a probability on the choice and an attenuverter and an offset on each of the two signals

params.text: Adds a fixed voltage to the HIGH signal, -5V to 5V. With nothing patched into the HIGH input this knob alone sets the HIGH voltage
Attenuverts the HIGH input, -1 to 1, before the HIGH offset knob is added to it
Adds a fixed voltage to the LOW signal, -5V to 5V. With nothing patched into the LOW input this knob alone sets the LOW voltage
Attenuverts the LOW input, -1 to 1, before the LOW offset knob is added to it
Chooses gate, where HIGH is passed while the gate is above 1V; latch, where each gate trigger sets the output to HIGH or to LOW; or toggle, where each gate trigger flips between them
Sets the probability of the choice coming out HIGH, 0 at the counter-clockwise end and 1 at the clockwise end; in toggle mode it is the probability of flipping at a trigger

inputs.text: The signal passed while HIGH is chosen; the number of channels here sets the number of channels at the output while HIGH is chosen
The signal passed while LOW is chosen; the number of channels here sets the number of channels at the output while LOW is chosen
The gate. Above 1V in gate mode the HIGH signal is passed, and in latch and toggle mode each rise above 2V is a trigger
Adds to the p knob, 0.1 of probability per volt, and the sum is held between 0 and 1

outputs.text: The chosen signal, clamped to -10V to 10V

notes: with nothing patched into the HIGH and LOW inputs both read 0V, so the module puts out its two offset knobs alone, switched by the gate.
the module comes up in gate mode with the p knob at 1, which passes the HIGH signal whenever the gate is above 1V and the LOW signal otherwise.
a gate is counted as a trigger when it rises above 2V and is released below 0.1V, while the level test in gate mode passes HIGH whenever the gate is above 1V.
there are two lamps: the upper one lights green while the HIGH signal is being passed and the lower one lights green while the LOW signal is being passed.
neither input nor the output was given a name in the code, so hovering one of them shows no description of what it carries.
